centered-guides.json.target: SmoothieBox exterior STEP/DIR contacts feed differential transmitters into the Delta DB44 peripherals. Each axis has a separate isolated ENABLE stage; retain motor/encoder/brake/STO power domains and qualify the spindle and cabinet interfaces independently.
centered-guides.json.plan: Original machine uses separate motor power stages. Keep their motor-power/phase/encoder wiring; connect SmoothieBox exterior command contacts through the shown candidate interfaces after the listed electrical and fitted-revision checks. Chapter 18 is a proposed case harness, not an as-built rating certificate. Selected architecture: SmoothieBox exterior case contacts with retained external power stages. The main diagram and connection-ID schedule define the current proposed routes. Dotted function-coloured GUESS routes need the named commissioning checks; OPEN routes remain disconnected until the missing terminal, rating or interface is established. Previous Core alternatives remain only in the superseded historical architecture record.

U/V/W are example motor phases; motor identity, cable contacts, encoder, brake and STO remain unresolved. PE is protective earth, never SmoothieBox logic GND or DC return. target_options.smoothiebox: Use a SmoothieBox enclosure with V2 Core. It must expose Core J5 STEP/DIR and 3.3V/GND connections to the differential line-driver board; it does not replace the servo drive power stages.
target_options.core: Recommended control target: V2 Core plus two TI AM26LV31E chips (or a reviewed rated isolated differential module) to drive the B3A-L differential pulse/sign pins. Validate voltage, line common, pulse mode, output power budget and cable fault behavior.
target_options.prime: Prime integrated stepper stages cannot replace the Delta AC servo drives. Prime GPIO breakout is not established as equivalent to the proposed Core differential drive interface; retain servo drives and use a suitable Core-based control interface.

parts: Two TI AM26LV31E quad 3.3V differential line drivers for six STEP/DIR channels; verify Core J5.10 current budget or use a separate regulated 3.3V supply. Each chip local 0.1µF decoupling, G pin4 high and /G pin12 low.

Three shielded twisted differential pairs per axis as a reviewed cable design; owner used stranded shielded Cat6 in this installation and reports a short that damaged the original DIR output, so inspect/continuity-test before reuse.
Isolated, 24V-rated digital output/input modules only after exact B3A-L DI/DO parameter and NPN/PNP mode is confirmed; pin 9 default SON is not a safety-rated input.
Retain exact Delta B3 drives/motors, encoder cables, Z brake circuit, STO/E-stop relay/contactors and machine earth.
Shared isolated servo-on proposal: ULN2003AN DIP16, AQY212GS SOP4, 390Ω LED resistor, 10kΩ pull-down; verified shared 24V DI supply. Fault/STO/brake remain independent model-matched circuits.
instructions: Read the model suffix on all X/Y/Z/spindle Delta drives. Confirm they are B3A-L pulse-type drives; the same-family pin numbers are not portable to other variants.

With power isolated, check every DB44 conductor for continuity, shorts between differential pair members and shorts to shields; the owner reported a crossed/melted X DIR pair that damaged a Mesa output and proximity switch.

Implement AM26LV31E diff outputs with exact pin assignments shown. Verify VCC/GND, both enable polarities, idle state and pulse pair with oscilloscope before connecting drives; test one axis while mechanically uncoupled/drive disabled.
Set/read back P1.000 differential command mode and pulse format. Do not connect 24V PULL_HI pins 35/36 in line-driver mode; never apply 24V to SIGN/PULSE pair contacts.

Read back DI/DO assignments and polarity before enabling SON/alarm/reset. Confirm safe E-stop/STO, limit switches and proximity inputs independently; do not repeat unattended homing until fault cause is corrected.
Keep servo AC, U/V/W, encoder, brake, STO and protective earth in the exact Delta machine wiring domain, never on Smoothie pins.
